Question: Do flight attendants ever get tips from first class passengers for exemplary service?
Answer: I was galley manager on that flight from London to a particular city in middle east. I had heard my supervisor brief us that we are expecting a VVIP group (members of the royal family) travelling with us. I thought nothing much of it as it's quite usual on that route. Somewhere middle of the flight I went in the cabin to check with customers who are awake if they would wanna get some beverages or snacks. While getting to know how their flight was going, I got into a conversation with this lady and came to know that they are bringing in her 11 years old little brother back from London after 3 years where he was admitted for cancer. He was 8 years when he was admitted and had a machine fixed somewhere in his lungs to help him breath which was finally removed a few months ago. It would be after 3 years that he would be sleeping in his own bed in his own house without any nurse or doctor supervising him once in a while and without any life support machines surrounding him. That hit me hard. So I went to galley and made a special dessert presentation plate for this kid which said, “Welcome back home, Live Long Life.” I checked with the lady if it's okay for him to consume the contents of that presentation plate and she gave us a thumbs up. It was just chocolate cake and some fruits. Somewhere in between I believe I saw her wipe some tears as well. The young man was super excited to have all the crew come up to him with the chocolate goodies and stuff and licked the plate clean within minutes. We felt happy and blessed to be able to make his flight home a little more special for him and that was it for us. At least for me. In about 5 minutes I got a call bell from that lady and went to check on her. She extended her hand and told me, “thank you for doing what you did, he is very happy” and the way she held her hand I knew she was holding onto something which she wanted to give me and I politely thanked her for her gesture and took a small step back to hint that I would have to decline her kind gift as it's not allowed by our airline to accept any tips. I folded my hands in Namaste and just as I was about to leave I saw her facial expressions change to somewhat disappointment and hurt. In a fraction of a second the sweet and calm in her eyes changed to confusion and hurt. I knew it then that that refusal of mine hurt her sentiments so to i went ahead and accepted what she was offering and upon going back to my galley realised it's the highest value currency note of this particular country which is almost about 150 usd. I immediately went back to her to tell her that I cannot accept it as it's a very big amount but she was just not ready to listen. I thanked her for her generosity and holding on to something which serves as a reminder of having made a positive impact on someone's life at that moment made me very happy. Till date I have never considered it as a currency note. It's more like an emotional note with good memory to it. Eventually I accepted it and to this day have it in my file of achievements along with other certificates of excellence. I hope I never have to use it ever. Coming back to the flight, we landed, parked and opened doors to see 4 Audis with a brigade of chauffeurs waiting to receive this particular family. They bid farewell and the lady again thanked us one more time before bidding farewell. Best wishes.
